channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: A pedra no sapato que o Centrão vê na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Centrão leaders assess that although Flávio Bolsonaro's meeting with Donald Trump was initially viewed positively, recent U.S. measures — including the designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations and the proposal of new tariffs — are being easily linked to him, creating a political liability. They argue the impact will depend on whether these measures actually harm Brazil's economy; if not, they won't significantly affect his campaign. However, his unexplained ties to Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master could become a future liability in polling.

item.title: O cálculo de Lula e o risco de Flávio após a nova ofensiva de Trump
item.description: Lula is leveraging the new U.S. tariffs as a political weapon against Flávio Bolsonaro, accusing him of promoting measures that harm Brazil and constituting treason, while avoiding direct confrontation with Trump. While the Planalto pressures the senator politically, Itamaraty maintains discreet diplomatic channels with Washington to preserve bilateral ties. Flávio’s trip to the U.S. to strengthen ties with the White House has backfired, as the tariffs now expose him as aligned with an agenda damaging Brazilian interests.

item.title: Moraes vota para rejeitar recurso de Roberto Jefferson contra multa de R$ 452 mil
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes voted to reject an appeal by former federal deputy Roberto Jefferson against a R$ 452,300 fine imposed by the judge. The ruling on the regimental appeal began this Friday, the 5th, and continues in the Court’s virtual plenary.

item.title: Crusoé: Messias vai para onde Deus mandar
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias stated during the 34th March for Jesus in São Paulo that he would accept a second nomination from President Lula to the Supreme Federal Court only if it aligns with God’s will, saying: 'When God commissions, He prepares. He sends.' The remark was made in response to a question about his willingness to fill a vacancy on the STF.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro pede ao STF que declare Moraes suspeito para julgar Vorcaro e caso Master
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro asked the STF to declare Justice Alexandre de Moraes as biased in the case involving Daniel Vorcaro and Banco Master, alleging a relationship between Moraes and the imprisoned businessman. The defense claims that the R$80 million paid by Master to Moraes' wife's law firm justifies the challenge, and requests that the investigation request by congressman Lindbergh Farias be reassigned to Justice André Mendonça.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio dá pontapé inicial com jingle 'Vem com Fé' em ritmo sertanejo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign kicked off with the release of the jingle 'Vem com Fé', in a sertanejo rhythm, produced by his new marketing team. The move signals the start of his communication strategy for the 2026 elections. The full article is available only to subscribers after registration.

item.title: Lula sanciona medida que autoriza renovação automática de CNH para 'bom condutor'; saiba o que muda
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional measure allowing automatic renewal of the driver's license (CNH) for drivers with no point-scoring infractions in the last 12 months, while maintaining mandatory medical exams. The measure aims to simplify the process, reduce administrative costs for Detrans, and enable exclusively digital issuance, with the physical version remaining optional. The proposal was approved following a congressional agreement that preserved the medical exam requirement.

item.title: O candidato que cresce nas pesquisas e vira dor de cabeça para a direita no duelo Lula x Flávio
item.description: Renan Santos, cofounder of MBL, rose from 2.4% to 6.9% in AtlasIntel polls for the 2026 presidential election, leading among voters aged 16–24 with 36.1% and showing the lowest rejection rate. However, his viability as a third way is constrained by the strength of Lulism and Bolsonarism, according to Laryssa Borges. His critical stance toward Bolsonaro distinguishes him from Caiado and Zema, who maintain ties with Bolsonaro’s base.

item.title: Mais de 70 mulheres tiveram mandatos cassados em 10 anos no país
item.description: Between 2015 and 2025, 71 women in Brazil had their mandates revoked or faced cassation proceedings, with a sharp increase starting in 2019. City councilwomen are the primary victims (73%), and nearly 40% of targeted legislators are from the PT or Psol, while those filing cassation requests are predominantly from right-wing and center-right parties (70%). The report identifies this as a political-ideological backlash against progressive women.

item.title: Flávio afirma que Pix é do Bolsonaro apesar de ex-presidente ter dito desconhecer a medida em 2020
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) claims his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was responsible for creating Pix, the Central Bank's instant payment system, despite the former president stating in 2020 that he was unaware of the measure. The statement comes amid efforts to distance himself from criticism of Pix and new U.S.-imposed tariffs. Flávio seeks to associate the Pix legacy with his father to bolster his political image amid international regulatory scrutiny.

item.title: Flávio quer suspeição de Moraes para julgar pedido para investigar elo com Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) has requested the recusal of Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, alleging Moraes has ties to Banco Master, to block Moraes from reviewing a petition to include Flávio’s alleged receipt of R$134 million from banker Daniel Vorcaro — funds allegedly used to finance the 'Dark Horse' film and possibly channeled through a Texas fund linked to Eduardo Bolsonaro — into the inquiry investigating Eduardo’s alleged obstruction of justice via international pressure on Brazilian authorities.

item.title: Como o governo pode reverter ‘crise’ por classificação de PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: The Lula government is assessing ways to prevent the U.S. designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations from escalating into a diplomatic crisis with the Trump administration. Advisors believe Lula and Trump may meet during the upcoming G7 summit in France, where the Brazilian president could propose enhanced cooperation against organized crime — without permitting U.S. intervention in Brazilian territory. Ministers have accelerated talks with U.S. officials to gauge the immediate effects of the decision, which is currently seen as more symbolic than operational.

item.title: Moraes vota pela rejeição de recurso de Roberto Jefferson contra multa de R$ 452 mil
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes voted to reject Roberto Jefferson's appeal against a R$ 452,000 fine for charges including slander, homophobia, and incitement to undermine the democratic state. The fine can be paid in 24 installments of R$ 18,800, and its payment is required for prison regime progression. Jefferson is currently serving house arrest with an electronic ankle monitor after a 2024 conviction for inciting Senate invasion and advocating the destruction of the TSE.

item.title: Leia todas as reportagens e veja os vídeos do 14º Fórum de Lisboa
item.description: The 14th Lisbon Forum, held in June 2026 at FDUL and promoted by Minister Gilmar Mendes, adopted a more global focus with record international speakers and fewer Brazilian authorities due to the election year. Speakers including Alexandre de Moraes, Luiz Fux, Michel Temer, and Rodrigo Pacheco debated AI regulation, social media governance, disinformation, technological sovereignty, and democratic risks, highlighting concerns about AI abuse in elections and attacks on Brazil’s Pix system and electoral integrity.

item.title: “Esbanja”: pesquisa mostra que 52% desaprovam atuação de Janja no governo Lula
item.description: A PoderData survey shows 52% of Brazilians disapprove of First Lady Rosângela Lula da Silva, known as Janja, in her role within the Lula government, while only 31% approve. Her increasing involvement in official agendas and internationally funded trips has drawn public criticism, seen as excessive or inappropriate.

item.title: Caiado muda discurso e nega chance de chapa única com Zema: ‘Vou continuar com a minha campanha’
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado denied the possibility of forming a single ticket with Romeu Zema for the 2026 elections, stating that each will continue with their individual campaigns. He clarified that talks with Zema and Flávio Bolsonaro aim only to prevent fragmentation of the center-right in the runoff to defeat the PT, not to unify candidacies in the first round. These statements contrast with earlier remarks when both suggested a potential union.

item.title: Análise da Viraliza debate regras eleitorais de 2026
item.description: The 2026 election requires a reconfiguration of digital marketing strategies due to stricter TSE regulations, particularly regarding influencer-based political propaganda. Viraliza Entretenimento warns that the fine line between spontaneous opinion and illegal propaganda is now a critical focus, making audits and strict compliance mandatory to avoid legal penalties and reputational damage. Short-form video content influences young voters, but paying influencers for political messaging, using paid boosting, or improper demonetization is prohibited, with shared responsibility placed on creators and brands.

item.title: PT CAI EM DESESPERO após Ciro DESISTIR e CERCAR LULA!!!
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) is facing internal crisis after Ciro Gomes withdrew from the 2026 presidential race, increasing the political isolation of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Ciro's candidacy could have drawn votes from the center and moderate left, acting as a potential counterweight to the strengthening of bolsonarism. His withdrawal leaves the PT more vulnerable and without competitive alternatives to defeat the right in 2026.

item.title: Postura de Flávio Bolsonaro é de “traidor”, diz líder do governo
item.description: Senate government leader Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) of asking U.S. President Donald Trump to 'punish' Brazil by supporting a proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian exports. Wagner labeled this stance as 'traitorous'. The statement comes amid growing trade tensions between Brazil and the United States.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1 e jornada de 40 horas dividem o Brasil antes da votação no Senado, segundo Le Figaro
item.description: The PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule and establishing a 40-hour workweek began its process in the Senate’s Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) next week, following approval in the Chamber. The issue has sparked intense national debate, dividing opinions among workers, unions, and productive sectors over impacts on productivity, employment, and quality of life. Le Figaro highlights that the matter has become one of the main polarization points in Brazil ahead of the Senate vote.

item.title: Juntos no palco, separados nas redes: Tarcísio ignora Flávio em postagens sobre a Marcha Para Jesus
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Flávio Bolsonaro reunited at the March for Jesus in São Paulo, but maintained distance on social media: the governor did not mention or feature the senator in his posts, while Flávio shared photos with Tarcísio. The relationship remains cold due to mutual distrust, particularly after the Banco Master case, despite expectations of rapprochement ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Dados e eleições
item.description: Despite strong economic indicators under Lula’s third term — including record-low unemployment, GDP growth above G20 averages, and poverty reduction — many voters still perceive the economy as worsening. This reflects a disconnect between objective macroeconomic performance and subjective experiences of social mobility, driven by persistent inflation in consumer memory, household debt (including online betting), comparisons to Lula’s earlier administrations, heightened consumption aspirations from social media, and the frustration of an educated generation that finds diplomas no longer guarantee upward mobility.

item.title: Daniel Vilela lidera disputa para o governo de GO em Goiânia
item.description: Daniel Vilela leads the race for governor of Goiás among voters in Goiânia with 35.20% of voting intentions, followed by Marconi Perillo with 19.40%, according to a Directa Pesquisas survey conducted between May 24 and 26, 2026. The poll interviewed 1,500 people aged 16 or older, has a margin of error of 2.53 percentage points, and is registered with the TSE under code GO-07758/2026.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro ressuscita em Lula o bordão ‘ianques, go home!’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro sought political momentum by aligning with Donald Trump, celebrating their White House meeting as a sign of international recognition. However, the same visit coincided with Trump announcing new tariffs on Brazilian goods, creating a contradiction between symbolic support and real economic harm. This ambiguity undermines his effort to position himself as a viable candidate, as Brazilian voters and businesses face economic pressure while their alleged ally celebrates the meeting.

item.title: EUA oficializam classificação de CV e PCC como organizações terroristas e medida entra em vigor
item.description: The United States officially designated the Comando Vermelho (CV) and Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) as terrorist organizations, in a notice signed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and effective Friday, May 5. The move, announced without prior notice to the Brazilian government, followed a request from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and authorizes asset freezes in the U.S., raising concerns about implications for Brazilian sovereignty and bilateral intelligence cooperation.

item.title: PCC e CV passam a ser considerados terroristas pelos EUA nesta sexta; entenda o que muda
item.description: The U.S. has designated Brazil's PCC and CV as terrorist groups effective Friday, granting American authorities enhanced power to investigate and disrupt their international financial operations, including money laundering via real estate, luxury assets, and shell companies. The move aims to freeze illicit assets and identify perpetrators without requiring coordination with the Brazilian government.

item.title: Governo monitora decisão dos EUA sobre PCC e CV em meio a preocupação com sanções financeiras e soberania
item.description: The Brazilian government is monitoring the U.S. decision to designate PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations, concerned about potential financial sanctions and impacts on national sovereignty. Diplomats and security officials are analyzing three scenarios: symbolic effect, Venezuelan-style asset seizures, or Mexican-style banking sanctions targeting money laundering. The primary concern is the replication of financial sanctions against institutions linked to organized crime, which could affect individuals, companies, and economic structures suspected of supporting these groups.

item.title: Prefeito de BH cancela viagem aos EUA durante a Copa após críticas
item.description: Belo Horizonte Mayor Álvaro Damião (União Brasil) canceled a planned trip to the United States scheduled to coincide with the start of the 2026 World Cup following public criticism. The trip, intended to attend an international event on early childhood development with expenses covered by organizers, was deemed inappropriate given the tournament timing. Damião stated he would remain in the city to oversee local infrastructure projects, declaring: 'Here is our World Cup'.

item.title: Ruptura entre Lula e Alcolumbre se aprofunda, após provocações do chefe do Planalto
item.description: The rupture between President Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has deepened after Lula provoked Alcolumbre during a ministerial meeting, blaming him for the conflict over the rejected STF nomination of Jorge Messias. Alcolumbre counters that Lula refuses to accept legislative defeat and is maintaining the feud for political gain, especially ahead of the Senate leadership election. Neither side shows willingness to meet and reconcile.

item.title: ‘Se me prenderem e o Brasil mudar, estou satisfeito’, afirma Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential pre-candidate for the Novo party, said he does not fear imprisonment or penalties from the PGR over satirical videos linking STF ministers to the Banco Master case, stating 'if they jail me and Brazil changes, I am very satisfied'. He accused the Supreme Court of losing credibility and aligning with corrupt figures, vowing to continue his criticism despite judicial pressure.

item.title: Desaprovação de Janja cai, mas ainda atinge 52% dos que a conhecem
item.description: Disapproval of First Lady Rosângela Lula da Silva, known as Janja, decreased by 9 percentage points since September 2025, falling from 61% to 52% among the 87% of Brazilians who know her. Despite the decline, over half of those familiar with her still disapprove of her government role, while 31% approve and 17% are undecided. The PoderData survey, conducted May 30–June 1, 2026, shows Janja remains one of the most controversial assets of Lula’s government, with her international travel and spending transparency influencing public perception.

item.title: SobeDesce: de Candido Portinari a Gustavo Petro
item.description: Candido Portinari will have his first major exhibition in Asia, with 50 works displayed at the National Museum of China, potentially attracting 4 million visitors. Rock in Rio 2026 recorded its highest pre-sale ever, selling out all tickets in just two hours. João Fonseca reached the quarterfinals at Roland Garros, the best result by a Brazilian since 2004. Gustavo Petro, Colombia’s leftist president, alleged election fraud after the right-wing opposition won the first round, despite conclusions from 200 international observers. Correios posted a BRL 3.2 billion loss in Q1 2026, nearly double the BRL 1.7 billion loss in the same period of 2025. HBO canceled Euphoria after its third season, which had faced criticism.

item.title: Ruídos eleitorais
item.description: Lula believes he has more adversaries in Washington than in Brasília following unsuccessful meetings with Trump and favorable reception of Flávio Bolsonaro by U.S. officials. He criticizes Marco Rubio for designating Brazilian criminal groups as terrorist organizations, which heightens legal and financial risks for Brazil, and views this as part of a strategy to bolster Bolsonaro’s prospects in the 2026 elections.

item.title: O impacto externo e as eleições
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections are heavily shaped by external factors, including the U.S. trade war, geopolitical competition for rare earths, and the designation of Brazilian criminal groups as terrorists. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are leveraging this context, as the U.S. oscillates between diplomatic engagement and punitive measures, while China waits for Brazil-U.S. tensions to escalate. Security and perceptions of leniency toward organized crime dominate electoral discourse, with opposing narratives of U.S. imperialism and government complicity with crime.

item.title: Ação que pede cassação de registro do PCO vai completar um ano sem movimentação no TSE
item.description: A lawsuit filed by the Electoral Public Ministry seeking to annul the registration of the PCO (Workers’ Cause Party) has remained stalled at the TSE for nearly a year, with no procedural movement. Filed in May 2025, the case has seen no rulings or scheduled hearings, suggesting possible internal delays or low prioritization by the court. If granted, the annulment would bar the party from contesting the 2026 elections.

item.title: Câmara escanteia comissões temáticas e aprova quase tudo sob urgência desde 2015
item.description: Between 2011 and 2025, over 96% of bills approved in the Chamber of Deputies advanced without undergoing full thematic committee review, due to the increasing use of the urgency regime, which shifted from exception to routine. In five of those years, every bill was voted on directly in plenary, a trend legislative consultants describe as a 'clear hypertrophy' of the urgency system and an erosion of deliberative quality, despite rising legislative output.

item.title: A nova pesquisa presidencial da Quaest, a primeira depois do tarifaço de Trump
item.description: The Quaest institute begins a presidential poll this Friday, interviewing 2,004 Brazilians in person through Monday, with results expected to be released on Wednesday, the 10th. This is the first poll conducted after the announcement of U.S. import tariffs by the Trump administration, which triggered global economic repercussions and may shape the electoral debate in Brazil. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Meme que pede prisão do clã Bolsonaro passa despercebido em processo de Trump contra Pix
item.description: A meme calling for the arrest of Jair Bolsonaro, Flávio Bolsonaro, and other members of the Bolsonaro clan was included among nearly 300 contributions submitted to the U.S. Trade Representative's (USTR) public consultation on Pix and other economic sectors, but went unnoticed. The exclusive subscriber-only article notes the inclusion occurred in the context of a U.S. investigation that could lead to 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods.

item.title: Temor do STF pesa na escolha de Bolsonaro de candidato ao Senado no RJ
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro is considering Sóstenes Cavalcante, the government leader in the Chamber of Deputies, as his Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro, praising his ability to build dialogue and political support. However, Bolsonaro fears that Cavalcante could become a target of new actions by the Supreme Federal Court (STF), which might jeopardize his candidacy. The decision reflects Bolsonaro’s concern about the vulnerability of his allies to judicial scrutiny.

item.title: O país que queremos: entre arrecadar mais e gastar menos, ajuste fiscal desafia próximo governo
item.description: The article discusses the fiscal adjustment challenge in Brazil, balancing the need to increase revenue with reducing spending to improve public accounts. It is part of a series by O GLOBO on economic issues relevant to the 2026 presidential election, based on columns by economist Fabio Giambiagi. The content is exclusive to subscribers and underscores the importance of economic policy for the next government.

item.title: ‘Expulsar o mal’ e ‘comício’: apesar de promessa, Marcha para Jesus vira embate político entre Flávio e governo Lula
item.description: The March for Jesus in São Paulo turned into a political battleground between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who accused the Lula government of representing the 'world of evil,' and President Lula, who justified his absence by stating he does not want to use religious events for political gain. Despite promises of non-partisanship, the event was used as a platform by Flávio, echoing his father Jair Bolsonaro’s 2022 rhetoric of a 'war between good and evil,' while Lula reiterated his commitment to religious neutrality during elections.

item.title: PL triplica fundo eleitoral em quatro anos, e Flávio e Lula terão quase 1/3 do recurso público para campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's PL party tripled its access to the electoral fund from 2022 to 2026, rising from R$ 288.5 million to R$ 881.6 million, while Lula's PT saw a modest increase from R$ 503.4 million to R$ 615.4 million. Seven parties now control over 70% of the R$ 4.9 billion fund, placing PL and PT at the top, with the Centrón bloc also strong. Despite the bolsonarist surge, the PT is now in a relative financial disadvantage after previously being the top recipient.

item.title: Deputados governistas vão aos EUA pedir investigação de Flávio
item.description: Four pro-government deputies traveled to Washington to urge U.S. authorities to open a money laundering investigation against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for president. The delegation, led by Pedro Uczai (PT-SC) and including Jandira Feghali (PCdoB-RJ), Pedro Campos (PSB-PE), and André Janones (Avante-MG), also requested the cancellation of U.S. tariffs on Brazil, claiming Bolsonaro is behind them to gain electoral advantage.

item.title: Janja mostra Lula fazendo exercício: “Feriadão nesse pique”
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva shared Instagram videos of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, exercising during the Corpus Christi holiday, including treadmill running and ankle mobility drills. The posts aim to showcase the president’s health as he campaigns for a fourth term, especially given he will turn 81 after the 2026 election runoff. Such content is routinely used to reassure voters about his fitness for office.

item.title: Governo quer reforçar mote de cooperação com EUA mesmo com revés de classificação de PCC e CV como terroristas
item.description: The Lula government seeks to strengthen cooperation with the U.S. despite the Trump administration's designation of CV and PCC as terrorist organizations, emphasizing existing efforts against organized crime and intelligence sharing. The strategy includes updating bilateral agreements and keeping the issue on the government's agenda to demonstrate commitment to international security.

item.title: Governo Lula tenta negociar com EUA até 15 de julho para evitar tarifaço: veja setores quem podem ser incluídos nas conversas
item.description: The Lula government has set July 15 as a definitive deadline to negotiate with the United States and avoid a 25% tariff on Brazilian products. Ongoing talks aim to find alternatives to prevent the so-called 'tariff hike' that could impact multiple sectors of the national economy.

item.title: Classificação do PCC e do CV como terroristas pelos EUA passa a valer a partir desta sexta-feira
item.description: Starting this Friday (5), the U.S. government designates Brazil's Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV) as terrorist organizations, enabling financial sanctions, visa restrictions, and asset freezes, though it does not change Brazilian law. Brazil is engaging diplomatically to reverse the decision, while U.S. officials state there are no plans for military operations in the country.

item.title: A estratégia já usada por Jair Bolsonaro contra Lula em 2022 e que Flávio decidiu repetir
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro participated in the March for Jesus in São Paulo and framed the 2026 election as a 'spiritual war' against evil, repeating the narrative used by Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. According to columnist Diogo Schelp, this strategy portrays the opponent as a moral threat to be eliminated, characterizing tribal polarization and radicalism, which amplifies political tensions.

item.title: Com programação paralela de festas temáticas, Parada LBGT+ leva Pabllo Vittar à av. Paulista
item.description: São Paulo's LGBT+ Pride Parade reaches its 30th edition in 2026 under the theme 'the street calls, the ballot confirms', linking the celebration of diversity to the election year. The event features 14 sound trucks with performances by Pabllo Vittar, Gloria Groove, Melody, and other artists, along with live coverage on DiaTV and parallel events such as Gongada Drag and RuPaul’s DragCon Brasil.

item.title: Messias diz que não viu Flávio na Marcha e que estava 'concentrado em Jesus'
item.description: The chief minister of the AGU, Jorge Messias, said he had no interaction with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during the March for Jesus, despite both being on the main sound truck. They remained in opposite corners of the vehicle, and Messias stated he was 'focused on Jesus' during the event.
